 AWAR D Preface 1.
Detailed Accident Report (DAR) has been filed seeking compensation for death of victim in motor vehicle accident.
Background 2.

Brief facts gleaned from DAR read with Final Report under section 279/304A IPC are that Daya Chand walking along the main Road near Taj Vivanta Hotel, Sector-21, Dwarka was hit by Hyundai i-10 Car No. DL-2CAE-8357 driven at high speed in rash and negligent manner on 06.07.2018 at about 9:30 am resulting in bodily injuries.
He was shifted to Ayushman MACT No.758/2018 Rajesh Kumar.
Vs. Prerna & Anr.
3. FIR No.182/2018 under section 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Sector-23, Dwarka on 06.07.2018 and statement of 'Caller' Ram Babu was recorded by the IO.

Respondent Ms. Prerna Jha (driver-cum-owner) was formally arrested & released on police bail and dead body of deceased was handed over to its relatives after identification and postmortem examination.

Offending Hyundai i-10 Car recovered from the spot was released on superdari after its mechanical inspection and documents including DL, RC & Insurance Policy of the vehicle were verified from concerned authorities.

Offence under section 304A IPC was added on the basis of Postmortem Report No.1183/2018 prepared at DDU Hospital, Hari Nagar, New Delhi stating cause of death due to 'Cranio Cerebral Injury' (Head Injury) AND 'Haemorrhagic Shock due to Multiple Vital Organ Injuries' (Lungs) as a result of road traffic accident.
IO, thereafter, concluded investigation and prepared DAR which was filed in Court along with copy of Final Report under section 279/304A IPC.
Defence 4.
Respondent Prerna Jha (driver-cum-owner) has filed reply disputing averments of Detailed Accident Report (DAR).
5. Respondent Go Digit General Insurance Co. on its part has filed Legal Offer - (i) admitting Policy No.D000163978 of MACT No.758/2018 Rajesh Kumar.

sentences.text: Following observations in para 15 of aforesaid judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court being relevant are extracted herein below:
"15. In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied...."

19. Similar observation has been recorded by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 by holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Respondent Ms. Prerna Jha (driver-cum-owner) was formally arrested & released on police bail and dead body of deceased was handed over to its relatives after identification and postmortem examination.
Offending Hyundai i-10 Car recovered from the spot was released on superdari after its mechanical inspection and documents including DL, RC & Insurance Policy of the vehicle were verified from concerned authorities.
Offence under section 304A IPC was added on the basis of Postmortem Report No.1183/2018 prepared at DDU Hospital, Hari Nagar, New Delhi stating cause of death due to 'Cranio Cerebral Injury' (Head Injury) AND 'Haemorrhagic Shock due to Multiple Vital Organ Injuries' (Lungs) as a result of road traffic accident.
Petitioner Rajesh Kumar is therefore awarded interest @ 7.5% per annum upon compensation Rs.11,65,000/- (Rupees Eleven Lakhs & Sixty Five Thousand only) from the date of filing of DAR on 20.08.2018 till notice of deposit under Order XXI Rule 1 CPC to petitioner/counsel.
However, since Hyundai i-10 Car No. DL-2CAE-8357 was insured against Third Party Risk so, R2/Go Digit General Insurance Co.
being statutorily liable under Section 149 (1) of M.V.Act shall pay compensation amount with interest to Rajesh Kumar in the absence of any statutory defence under section 149(2) of M.V. Act.

Loss of Dependency 31. Loss of dependency is calculated as Rs.36,000/- x 5 x 12 x 1/2 = Rs.10,80,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs & Eighty Thousand only).
Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 59.8 of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi (Supra) decided on 31.10.2017 has laid down reasonable figures under the heads - (i) loss of estate; (ii) loss of consortium AND (iii) funeral expenses fixed as Rs.15,000/-;
Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively to be enhanced @ 10% after every three years.
A sum of Rs.18,150/- (Rupees Eighteen Thousand One Hundred Fifty only) is awarded to petitioner under the head - 'loss of estate' in terms of aforesaid judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
Similarly, another sum of Rs.18,150/- (Rupees Eighteen Thousand One Hundred Fifty only) is awarded to petitioner under the head - 'funeral expenses' in terms of the law/guidelines laid down in aforesaid case.

Ltd. vs Satinder Kaur (2021) 11 SCC 780, a sum of Rs.48,400 (Rupees Forty Eight Thousand & Four Hundred only) is awarded to Rajesh Kumar (son/LR of Late Daya Chand) as compensation under the head 'loss of consortium'.
